page.home.title: This page in short
page.home.what: Giftwise helps friends and family give to a person on SSI without lowering her monthly check.
page.home.why: Try the Gift Checker beside the headline, or take the 2-minute tour for a guided walk through every part.
page.home.technical: Landing page. The Gift Checker runs the same rules engine (v2026.1) in the browser that the API runs on the server.

hero.who.title: Who Giftwise is for
hero.who.what: People who receive SSI (Supplemental Security Income), the family and friends who help them, and the benefits counselors who advise them.
hero.who.why: About 7.3 million people receive SSI. Gifts are common, and the way a gift arrives decides whether it lowers the check.

gift-checker.about.title: Gift Checker
gift-checker.about.what: Type an amount and choose how it reaches her. The check updates right away.
gift-checker.about.why: It shows the difference between giving cash and paying a shop directly, using Social Security's 2026 numbers.
gift-checker.about.technical: Client-side call to evaluateGift() in src/lib/rules (deterministic, no AI). Sample profile: living alone, no other income, savings $1,240.

gift-checker.amount.title: Gift amount
gift-checker.amount.what: How much the gift is worth, in dollars.
gift-checker.amount.why: Larger cash gifts lower the check more. Payments to a shop are not counted at any size.

gift-checker.route.title: How the gift reaches her
gift-checker.route.what: Cash goes to her. Pay the shop means the giver pays the seller directly. Toward rent means family pays her rent.
gift-checker.route.why: Social Security counts cash as income, does not count payments made straight to a shop for her needs, and counts rent help as housing support.
gift-checker.route.technical: cash: R-CASH-01. Pay the shop: R-VEND-01 (20 CFR 416.1103(g), POMS SI 00815.400). Rent: R-SHEL-01, with R-ABLE-01 as the better route. PayPal Orders v2 with payee set to the vendor.

gift-checker.result.title: Her check
gift-checker.result.what: Her SSI payment after this gift. The 2026 full amount for one person is $994 a month.
gift-checker.result.why: Counted income lowers the check dollar for dollar after small exclusions.
gift-checker.result.technical: check = federal benefit rate minus countable income (after the $60 quarterly and $20 monthly exclusions).

gift-checker.rma.title: Why the change comes two months later
gift-checker.rma.what: Income counted in one month changes the check two months later.
gift-checker.rma.why: Social Security uses retrospective monthly accounting, so a gift in April affects the June check.
gift-checker.rma.technical: POMS SI 02005.001. Engine: payment month = income month + 2.

view.mode.title: Plain or Technical
view.mode.what: Plain shows short explanations in everyday words. Technical adds rule numbers, API calls and the tools used.
view.mode.why: Families and judges can read the same page at the level that suits them.

view.labels.title: Info labels
view.labels.what: Shows or hides the word "info" beside each i button.
view.labels.why: The i buttons always work. The label makes them easier to spot on a first visit.

view.theme.title: Theme
view.theme.what: System is the default: the site follows your device's light or dark setting. Light and Dark stay the same whatever the device says.
view.theme.why: Choose whichever is most comfortable to read.

view.text.title: Text size
view.text.what: Large makes all text about a fifth bigger.
view.text.why: Comfortable reading for everyone, including people with low vision.

stack.strip.title: Every tool, with a job
stack.strip.what: These are the tools Giftwise is built with. Each one does one specific job here.
stack.strip.why: Open any name to see what it does in Giftwise, or visit How it is built for where each one lives in the code.

stack.paypal.title: PayPal
stack.paypal.what: Moves the money: donors pay the shop directly, and every payment lands in her monthly ledger.
stack.paypal.why: Paying the shop instead of the person is what keeps her full check.
stack.paypal.technical: Orders v2 with a payee on each purchase unit, so one checkout can pay several recipients. JavaScript SDK v6 buttons, server-side capture with PayPal-Request-Id idempotency, approval links with a return capture for AI agents, Payouts batches for funds, Transaction Search and the Balances API for reconciliation, signature-verified webhooks, and sandbox negative testing. Sandbox only.

stack.paypal_apis.title: Every PayPal API Giftwise calls
stack.paypal_apis.what: Each PayPal API and tool in the code, the call it makes, and the one job it does here.
stack.paypal_apis.why: PayPal is how Giftwise works, not a button at the end: every gift, check, payout and receipt goes through these calls.
stack.paypal_apis.technical: Listed from the code, not from memory. The Orders calls for checkout go through @paypal/paypal-server-sdk; the rest use fetch with one cached OAuth token.

stack.claude.title: Claude Opus 5.5
stack.claude.what: Reads bills and quotes, finds the matching rule, and runs the two AI reviewers.
stack.claude.why: It does the reading and checking a benefits counselor would do, with a source for every answer.
stack.claude.technical: claude-opus-5-5 with adaptive thinking, vision, structured outputs (zod), and server-side fallbacks. The money math is done by deterministic code, never the model.

stack.ag-studio.title: AG Studio
stack.ag-studio.what: The dashboard of Maya’s year, and an assistant inside it that builds widgets and answers questions with the Giftwise rules engine.
stack.ag-studio.why: Families and counselors see at a glance that the help arrived and the check stayed whole, and can build their own views.
stack.ag-studio.technical: ag-studio 3.0 with two data sources on a shared calendar, a theme mapped to the site tokens, a custom Giftwise check widget, and the Studio Agent Framework: the five built-in agents run on Claude Haiku 5.5 through our own AgLlmAdapter, and the lead and data agents also get the rules engine as a tool.

stack.render.title: Render
stack.render.what: Hosts the site and its Postgres database, and checks the live demo from outside every night.
stack.render.why: A demo that is checked every night keeps working through judging, and any failure is found before a judge finds it.
stack.render.technical: render.yaml defines the web service, managed Postgres, the giftwise-checks Render Workflow (one task per check, run in parallel with retries) and a nightly cron job that starts it with the Render SDK's workflows.startTask. Tables are created by a pre-deploy command on every release.

stack.bryntum.title: Bryntum
stack.bryntum.what: The benefit calendar: every gift on its day, when each report is due, and the check each month pays.
stack.bryntum.why: SSI counts income by calendar month and quarter, so seeing gifts on a calendar shows why the day a gift arrives can matter.
stack.bryntum.technical: @bryntum/calendar 7.3.7 (trial) with the React wrapper. onDragMoveEnd reruns planMonths(); the move form gives the same result without dragging (WCAG 2.5.7).

stack.apimatic.title: APIMatic
stack.apimatic.what: Generated the PayPal Server SDK that Giftwise uses for every Orders call.
stack.apimatic.why: A typed SDK catches mistakes in PayPal requests before they reach PayPal.
stack.apimatic.technical: @paypal/paypal-server-sdk, generated by APIMatic, for creating, reading and capturing orders.

intro.rule.title: The rule behind Giftwise
intro.rule.what: When someone pays a shop directly for something she needs, other than housing, Social Security does not count it as her income.
intro.rule.why: The same gift sent as cash would be counted, so the way a gift arrives matters.
intro.rule.technical: 20 CFR 416.1103(g); POMS SI 00815.400 (Example 2: a sister pays the phone company).

how.steps.title: From a need to a payment
how.steps.what: A caregiver adds a need, Giftwise checks the rule, a donor pays the shop with PayPal, and her month stays steady.
how.steps.why: Each step shows its result, so everyone knows where things stand.
how.steps.technical: Claude vision extraction, the rules engine with cited sources, PayPal Orders v2 with a payee per purchase unit, server-side capture, and a hash-chained ledger.

showcase.board.title: Sample requests
showcase.board.what: Eight requests from a sample household and how Giftwise delivered each one. Select a row to see why.
showcase.board.why: Everyday needs each have a best route: pay the shop, give the item, or use her ABLE account.
showcase.board.technical: Each row runs evaluateGift() live with the 2026 rules.

rules.list.title: The seven numbers
rules.list.what: The 2026 amounts that decide most gift questions.
rules.list.why: Knowing them makes the rest of the rules easy to follow.

rules.limit.title: Savings limit
rules.limit.what: Countable savings must be $2,000 or less at the start of each month ($3,000 for a couple).
rules.limit.why: Cash kept past the end of the month counts toward this limit.

rules.fbr.title: Full SSI payment
rules.fbr.what: The most SSI pays one person in 2026 is $994 a month, before any state supplement.

rules.infrequent.title: One-off gift exclusion
rules.infrequent.what: The first $60 a quarter of one-off income, such as a single gift, is not counted.
rules.infrequent.why: Small occasional gifts usually leave the check unchanged.
rules.infrequent.technical: POMS SI 00810.410. Since July 2004 the first $60 is excluded even when the total is higher.

rules.gie.title: General exclusion
rules.gie.what: The first $20 of income each month is not counted.
rules.gie.why: It applies to most income, including cash gifts and housing support.

rules.pmv.title: Housing support cap
rules.pmv.what: When someone else pays her rent or utilities, the check goes down by at most $351.33 a month in 2026.
rules.pmv.why: Sending that money to her ABLE account instead keeps the full check.
rules.pmv.technical: Presumed maximum value, POMS SI 00835.901. Applies to shelter only since September 30, 2024.

rules.able-limit.title: ABLE yearly limit
rules.able-limit.what: Up to $20,000 a year can be added to an ABLE account, from everyone combined.
rules.able-limit.why: Giftwise tracks the total so gifts stay within it.
rules.able-limit.technical: 2026 limit; SSA Spotlight on ABLE accounts.

rules.able-balance.title: ABLE balance
rules.able-balance.what: The first $100,000 in an ABLE account does not count toward the $2,000 savings limit.
rules.able-balance.why: Gifts can build savings there without affecting SSI.

stats.example.title: A sample year
stats.example.what: Each bar is the help a sample household received in one month through Giftwise.
stats.example.why: Every gift was routed the benefit-safe way, so none of it was counted and her check stayed $994 every month.
stats.example.technical: Sample data. Each gift was evaluated with the rules engine (v2026.1); counted income was $0 in every month. Not a forecast for any real person.

research.row.title: Sources
research.row.what: The rules and research Giftwise is built on. Each name opens the original source.
research.row.why: Every answer in Giftwise can be traced back to these documents.

reach.row.title: Who it reaches
reach.row.what: Published counts from Social Security and the ABLE National Resource Center. Each figure links to its source.
reach.row.why: Help with housing changes the check for hundreds of thousands of people on SSI, and many more people can now open an ABLE account than have one.
reach.row.technical: 793,000 and its split (358,000 under the one-third reduction, 434,000 under the presumed maximum value) are SSA's estimate for January 2022 in 88 FR 9779. $0.41 billion is SSA's estimate of SSI overpayments from in-kind support and maintenance in FY 2024, as charted by the Inspector General (report 152601, Figure 5). ABLE counts are ABLE NRC's: more than 246,000 accounts and over $3.2 billion as of March 31, 2026; about 8 million eligible under the original law and an estimated 6 million more from January 1, 2026.

judges.invariants.title: Random gifts, every promise kept
judges.invariants.what: A program makes up gifts, needs and people at random, routes each gift, and checks every answer against twelve promises.
judges.invariants.why: Hand-written tests cover the cases someone thought of. Random ones cover the rest: odd amounts, many small needs, ABLE accounts near the limit, people with wages and other income.
judges.invariants.technical: src/lib/invariants.ts: a seeded mulberry32 generator, so the same seed gives the same cases. routeGift() is checked for cent conservation, check equal to the no-gift check, never below cash, need caps, ABLE yearly limit and eligibility, at most 10 PayPal purchase units, whole cents, rule ids from the rule table, checks within the federal rate, recomputation and determinism.

judges.rules_watch.title: The rules watch
judges.rules_watch.what: Giftwise asks the Federal Register for every change to SSI's income rules and yearly amounts, and lists what it does with each one.
judges.rules_watch.why: Rules and amounts change. SSA published the 2027 amounts on October 26, 2026, and January's checks already use them.
judges.rules_watch.technical: GET /api/rules-watch. Three queries to api.federalregister.gov (no key), matched by document number against content/rules-watch.json; any document not on the list is named and fails the nightly check. Under retrospective accounting the January and February checks use the new rate, and the one-third reduction and presumed maximum value follow it (POMS SI 02005.001 E.4.c).

dev.teaser.title: For developers
dev.teaser.what: Other apps can check any gift with one API call, or connect an AI agent through our MCP server.
dev.teaser.why: Giving platforms, ABLE programs and caseworker tools can make every gift benefit-safe.
dev.teaser.technical: POST /api/v1/check-gift, bearer key gw_test_..., OpenAPI 3.1, MCP at /api/mcp.

built.list.title: How it is built
built.list.what: Every tool in Giftwise and the one job it does.
built.list.why: Each tool is visible in the product, not just listed.

learnMore.label: Where each tool lives in the code

faq.list.title: Questions
faq.list.what: Short answers to what people ask most.
faq.list.why: Hover or tap a question to see its answer.

cta.dialog.title: Start a gift page
cta.dialog.what: Type the first name of the person the page is for. Giftwise builds the page from a fundraiser's list of needs, or from the sample.
cta.dialog.why: No sign-up is needed, and every payment runs in PayPal's sandbox.

page.learn.title: About this page
page.learn.what: Each section explains one rule in plain words, with a worked example and its source.
page.learn.why: Knowing these rules is how families give without lowering the check.
page.learn.technical: Worked examples are computed live by the rules engine (v2026.1). Technical mode shows rule IDs and manual sections.

page.try.title: About this page
page.try.what: Test Giftwise with your own situation, or open one of the ready-made examples.
page.try.why: You can see exactly how a gift would be counted before anyone sends money.
page.try.technical: Describe and CSV tabs run the deterministic engine. Bill and fundraiser tabs ask Claude Opus 5.5 to read the document. Nothing you enter is stored unless you save it.

try.describe.title: Describe a gift
try.describe.what: Enter the amount, what it is for, and how it would reach her.
try.describe.why: Giftwise shows her check and the best way to give.

try.csv.title: A month of gifts
try.csv.what: Upload or paste a list of gifts as CSV. A template is available to download.
try.csv.why: Several gifts in one quarter share the $60 exclusion, so the whole month matters.
try.csv.technical: POST /api/v1/plan-month. Columns: date, giver, amount, description, paid_to (person, shop, able, item), category, recurring.

try.bill.title: A bill or quote
try.bill.what: Upload or photograph a bill or a quote. Claude reads it and Giftwise checks the rule.
try.bill.why: Most needs start as a piece of paper. This turns it into a safe payment plan.
try.bill.technical: POST /api/v1/read-bill: Claude Opus 5.5 vision with a structured output schema, then the rules engine and its cited sources.

try.fundraiser.title: A fundraiser page
try.fundraiser.what: Paste a link to a public fundraising page. Giftwise reads it and shows how every dollar can reach her benefit-safe.
try.fundraiser.why: Fundraisers often raise cash, which counts as income. A plan can deliver the same help without lowering the check.
try.fundraiser.technical: POST /api/v1/analyze-fundraiser: Giftwise fetches the public page, Claude extracts the goal and what the money is for, and the engine plans benefit-safe routes.

try.presets.title: Ready-made examples
try.presets.what: Eight examples from a sample household. Open one to see the full result, or download its files to try them yourself.
try.presets.why: They cover the common cases: repairs, cash, utilities, rent, school, food, a fundraiser and a busy month.
try.presets.technical: Inputs and expected results live in content/presets. Downloads include the JSON input, the expected output and any sample documents.

try.profile.title: Her situation
try.profile.what: A few facts that change how gifts are counted.
try.profile.why: For example, living in someone else's home changes how housing help is counted.
try.profile.technical: Profile fields: couple, livesInAnothersHousehold, otherUnearnedMonthly, earnedMonthly, ableEligible, savings.

try.result.title: The result
try.result.what: Her check after this gift, the best way to give, and the rule behind it.
try.result.why: You can see the difference before choosing how to give.

page.gift.title: About this page
page.gift.what: This is a gift page. Each item is something Maya needs, and you pay for it straight to the shop with PayPal.
page.gift.why: Paying the shop directly is not counted as her income, so her SSI check stays the same.
page.gift.technical: Server creates a PayPal Orders v2 order with purchase_units[0].payee set to the shop's sandbox account, the PayPal JavaScript SDK v6 opens checkout, and the server captures it. Every step is written to the audit ledger.

gift.needs.title: Her needs
gift.needs.what: Things Maya needs right now. Each shows where the money goes and the rule that keeps her check whole.
gift.needs.why: Choosing a specific need means your gift arrives the benefit-safe way.
gift.needs.technical: Rows from the needs table; each is checked with evaluateGift() before an order is created, and the server refuses any route that would lower the check.

gift.route.vendor.title: Paid straight to the shop
gift.route.vendor.what: Your PayPal payment goes directly to the shop, not to Maya and not to Giftwise.
gift.route.vendor.why: Social Security does not count payments made directly to a shop for her needs, other than housing, as income.
gift.route.vendor.technical: PayPal Orders v2 'pay another account': payee.email_address is the vendor. Rule R-VEND-01, 20 CFR 416.1103(g), POMS SI 00815.400.

gift.route.able.title: Paid to her ABLE account
gift.route.able.what: Help with utilities or rent goes to her ABLE account, and she pays the bill from it in the same month.
gift.route.able.why: Utilities paid by someone else count as housing support. Money given to her ABLE account does not.
gift.route.able.technical: PayPal Orders v2 with payee set to the ABLE sandbox account. Rules R-ABLE-01 and R-ABLE-02, POMS SI 01130.740.

gift.month.title: Her month
gift.month.what: Her SSI check and what has been given this month.
gift.month.why: Every gift on this page is counted as $0 income, so her check stays the same.
gift.month.technical: Totals from captured payments in the database; counted income from the rules engine.

gift.any.title: Give any amount
gift.any.what: Type any amount. Giftwise splits it across her open needs, paid straight to each shop, and puts what is left in her ABLE account.
gift.any.why: The same money given as cash would lower her check. Routed this way, every dollar arrives and her check stays the same.
gift.any.technical: routeGift() fills open needs in order and checks every line with the rules engine; any line that would lower the check is skipped. The server rebuilds the plan, then creates one PayPal Orders v2 order with one purchase unit per payee, so one checkout pays every recipient.

gift.receipt.title: Public receipt
gift.receipt.what: Anyone with this link can see where the money went, which rule kept her check whole, and a live check against PayPal.
gift.receipt.why: A receipt you can check yourself is easier to trust than a promise.
gift.receipt.technical: Payments and audit events from the database. 'Check with PayPal' calls GET /v2/checkout/orders/{id} live; 'Verify the ledger' recomputes every SHA-256 hash in the audit chain.

gift.sandbox.title: Testing with PayPal sandbox
gift.sandbox.what: This demo uses PayPal's sandbox, a practice version of PayPal where no real money moves.
gift.sandbox.why: Anyone can try the full payment safely. Use the sandbox buyer login from TESTING.md in the project repository.
gift.sandbox.technical: api-m.sandbox.paypal.com and the sandbox JavaScript SDK at www.sandbox.paypal.com/web-sdk/v6/core.

real.world.title: How this works for real
real.world.what: What changes outside the sandbox: how a shop gets paid, how a gift reaches an ABLE account, and who pays the fees.
real.world.why: PayPal pays every recipient directly, so each one has to be a PayPal business account or an ABLE plan's own gift page.
real.world.technical: Answers in content/real-world.json. Each cites PayPal's developer docs, the IRS, SSA's operating manual or the ABLE plan's own page.

page.status.title: About this page
page.status.what: A live check of every service Giftwise uses: PayPal, Claude, the database and each sponsor tool.
page.status.why: If a service is not reachable, Giftwise uses its fallback so the demo keeps working. This page shows which mode each one is in.
page.status.technical: GET /api/health runs the same checks and returns JSON.

page.about.title: About this page
page.about.what: What Giftwise is, what it is not, how it handles your data, and credits.
page.about.why: So you know exactly what to expect before you use it.

page.judges.title: About this page
page.judges.what: A short path through Giftwise for judges, the failure cases run live, and the latest test results.
page.judges.why: So you can check every claim yourself in a few minutes.
page.judges.technical: The failure-case runner is POST /api/judges/run. It creates small PayPal sandbox orders and runs the same capture and order code the gift page uses.

judges.cases.title: Failure cases
judges.cases.what: Eight ways a gift can go wrong: seven run live against the PayPal sandbox, and one where an AI reviewer gets the rule wrong.
judges.cases.why: A payment product is only as good as what it does when something fails.
judges.cases.technical: Declines use PayPal's sandbox negative testing (PayPal-Mock-Response: INSTRUMENT_DECLINED). Double clicks share one PayPal-Request-Id. The ledger check edits a copy in memory, never the stored ledger. The reviewer case replays the recorded Electric bill review with one quote replaced, through the same referee code the API uses.

judges.tests.title: Test results
judges.tests.what: Each automated test suite, how many checks passed, and the command that runs it.
judges.tests.why: You can run the same commands from the repository and get the same results.
judges.tests.technical: Unit tests use Vitest. Browser checks use Playwright with real Chrome and axe-core.

page.developers.title: About this page
page.developers.what: Everything a developer needs to add benefit-safe giving checks to their own product: a free key, a live playground and code samples.
page.developers.why: Giving platforms, ABLE programs and AI agents can check a gift before it is sent.
page.developers.technical: Keys are gw_test_ plus 32 random bytes in base62. Only the SHA-256 hash is stored. Limits are counted per key in Postgres.

dev.keys.title: Sandbox keys
dev.keys.what: A free key for testing. It is shown once; Giftwise keeps only a fingerprint of it.
dev.keys.why: Keys give you higher limits and a usage page, and you can rotate or revoke them anytime.
dev.keys.technical: POST /api/keys returns the key once. Rotate and revoke are tied to this browser through an httpOnly cookie, with no passwords.

dev.playground.title: Playground
dev.playground.what: Send real requests to the live API and see the full response, plus the same call in cURL, JavaScript and Python.
dev.playground.why: You can see exactly what your code will get back before you write it.
dev.playground.technical: Requests go to the same endpoints your code will call, through the same key check and rate limits.

page.docs.title: About this page
page.docs.what: The reference for every endpoint: fields, examples, errors and limits.
page.docs.why: So you can build against the API without guessing.
page.docs.technical: Field tables are generated from the Zod schemas every request is validated with, the same source as /openapi.json.

page.keys.title: About this page
page.keys.what: The keys created in this browser, the calls they made, and buttons to rotate or revoke them.
page.keys.why: You stay in control of every key.
page.keys.technical: GET /api/keys reads usage from the api_requests table. Rotate issues a new key and revokes the old one in one step.

review.panel.title: Two reviewers, two rulebooks
review.panel.what: Two AI reviewers decide whether a bill is a housing cost. One reads only the federal regulations and the Federal Register. The other reads only Social Security’s operating manual.
review.panel.why: Housing paid by someone else lowers her check, so this one question decides where the money should go. Two independent readings, each with its quote checked, are harder to get wrong than one.
review.panel.technical: POST /api/v1/review-bill. Each reviewer is claude-opus-5-5 with a structured output whose passage_id is limited to its own rulebook. The referee is plain code: a quote must appear word for word in the passage it cites. Giftwise acts on a reading only when both checked answers agree; otherwise the rules engine picks the route with the best worst case.

review.regs.title: Regulations reviewer
review.regs.what: Reads only the federal regulations (20 CFR Part 416) and the Federal Register.
review.regs.why: The regulations are the law SSA applies. A second reviewer reads SSA’s manual, so each answer is checked against a different source.

review.poms.title: Manual reviewer
review.poms.what: Reads only Social Security’s Program Operations Manual System (POMS), the instructions SSA staff follow.
review.poms.why: The manual has the worked examples staff use day to day. Its answer is compared with the regulations reviewer’s.

try.makepage.title: Make a gift page
try.makepage.what: Turns what a fundraiser asks for into a live gift page. Givers pay each need through PayPal, straight to the shop or the ABLE account.
try.makepage.why: Money raised as cash counts as income and can lower the SSI check. The same help, paid to the shop, does not.
try.makepage.technical: POST /api/v1/gift-pages. The rules engine picks each route: housing goes to the ABLE account, everything else to the shop. Sandbox only; five pages a day per visitor.

page.agents.title: About this page
page.agents.what: How AI assistants use Giftwise: they check a gift before giving to someone on SSI, and can prepare a PayPal checkout that only the giver approves.
page.agents.why: More giving now starts with an assistant. A check the assistant can call keeps the gift from lowering someone’s monthly check.
page.agents.technical: Model Context Protocol over Streamable HTTP at /api/mcp, stateless JSON-RPC. Seven tools; five only read. start_gift_checkout creates a sandbox order the giver approves; start_monthly_gift saves a monthly plan the giver approves each month.

agents.demo.title: An assistant that asks first
agents.demo.what: A Claude assistant answering a real question from June, Maya’s aunt. It has no knowledge of SSI rules beyond what the Giftwise tools return.
agents.demo.why: It shows the whole path: what cash would do, the safer way, a PayPal checkout June approves herself, and PayPal’s own record of what that order pays.
agents.demo.technical: claude-opus-5-5 with adaptive thinking in a manual tool-use loop. Giftwise tools are discovered with tools/list and called with tools/call over HTTP to /api/mcp. paypal_get_order asks PayPal’s own MCP server: the @paypal/mcp package (PayPal Agent Toolkit), which Giftwise runs as a child process over stdio with a sandbox access token. PayPal’s hosted server (mcp.sandbox.paypal.com, SSE) is the second choice (github.com/paypal/AI-Toolkit/issues/34). GET /v2/checkout/orders/{id} answers when neither can.

agents.connect.title: Connect your agent
agents.connect.what: Add the Giftwise MCP server to Claude, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or any MCP client with one URL.
agents.connect.why: Any assistant can then check a gift before it gives.
agents.connect.technical: Streamable HTTP, protocol versions 2025-03-26 to 2025-11-25, JSON responses, no session. Rate limit 20 requests a minute per client.

judges.eval.title: The two reviewers, measured
judges.eval.what: 59 bills paid by someone else, each labeled from the rule text, run through Claude with no rulebook, each reviewer alone, and the two reviewers with the referee. The table shows how often each was right, and how often it accepted a route that would lower the check.
judges.eval.why: A claim about AI should come with a measurement. These numbers come from one recorded run, not from a description.
judges.eval.technical: scripts/run-eval.ts over content/eval/bills.json (20) and content/eval/bills-hard.json (39); results in content/eval-results.json. Accuracy counts only the 52 clear bills; a wrong route is one that lowers the check under the true reading, and for the 7 contested bills under either reading. --rescore re-scores the recorded answers without API calls.

judges.ssa_examples.title: Social Security's own examples
judges.ssa_examples.what: Worked examples from Social Security's operating manual, each with SSA's answer, run through Giftwise and through Claude with no rulebook.
judges.ssa_examples.why: Our own labeled bills show the code does what we meant. SSA's examples show whether it agrees with SSA.
judges.ssa_examples.technical: content/eval/ssa-examples.json (passages cut verbatim from the POMS pages), scored by scripts/run-ssa-examples.ts into content/eval/ssa-examples-results.json. A value matches within $1.

page.dashboard.title: About this page
page.dashboard.what: A dashboard of every gift to Maya this year: who gave, what it paid for, how it reached her, and her SSI check each month.
page.dashboard.why: Families and counselors can see at a glance that the help arrived and her check stayed whole, and what cash would have cost.
page.dashboard.technical: AG Studio 3.0. The Giftwise check is a custom widget that runs the rules engine on the filtered rows. In edit mode the AI Assistant is the Studio Agent Framework on Claude, through /api/studio-ai, with the rules engine added as the ssi_rules_engine tool.

page.organizations.title: About this page
page.organizations.what: How a foundation, mutual-aid fund or church that already holds money for families can pay many families’ needs at once.
page.organizations.why: A grant sent as cash can lower someone’s SSI check just like a gift. Paid to the shop or the ABLE account, it does not.
page.organizations.technical: PayPal Payouts: one batch, one item per payee, each grant routed by the rules engine. The Balances API shows the fund’s balance, and Transaction Search confirms each payout in PayPal’s own report.

org.fund.title: The sample fund
org.fund.what: A fictional fund. Its money sits in its own PayPal account, which in the sandbox is this app’s business account.
org.fund.why: Giftwise never holds the money. The fund pays each shop and ABLE account directly.
org.fund.technical: GET /v1/reporting/balances. PayPal refreshes this figure periodically, so it can lag a recent payout.

org.grants.title: Choose the grants
org.grants.what: Pick an amount for each household. Giftwise splits each one across that household’s open needs and ABLE account.
org.grants.why: Every line is checked by the rules engine, and a grant that would lower a check is not sent.
org.grants.technical: POST /api/org/payouts with preview: true returns the routing only. Sandbox limits keep the fund usable for everyone.

org.batch.title: The payout batch
org.batch.what: PayPal’s live status for every item in the batch, and whether it already appears in PayPal’s transaction report.
org.batch.why: The fund can show its board or its auditors exactly where every dollar went.
org.batch.technical: GET /v1/payments/payouts/{id} for item status and transaction ids; Transaction Search (/v1/reporting/transactions) to confirm each one. Paid items count toward their needs once, however often the batch is refreshed. Payout webhooks refresh it too.

page.manage.title: Manage a gift page
page.manage.what: The organizer's private view of a gift page: add, change or remove needs, see gifts as they arrive, share the page, get told about each gift, and close the page.
page.manage.why: Needs change. A family can keep the page right without an account, and Giftwise still chooses where every need is paid.
page.manage.technical: /manage/{token}. The token is 24 random characters, shown once when the page is made; only its SHA-256 is stored (households.manage_token_hash). API: GET and PATCH /api/manage/{token}, POST /needs, PATCH and DELETE /needs/{id}, PUT and POST /webhook.

manage.needs.title: Where each need is paid
manage.needs.what: You say what the need is and who sells it. Giftwise decides the route: housing (rent, utilities, mortgage, property tax) always goes to the ABLE account; everything else is paid straight to the shop.
manage.needs.why: Housing paid by someone else lowers the SSI check even when it is paid to the landlord, so the rules choose the route, not the form.
manage.needs.technical: routeNeed() in src/lib/manage.ts; every need's rule line comes from evaluateGift(). A need with gifts cannot be removed or lowered below what was paid, so its receipts keep pointing at it.

manage.notify.title: Gift notifications
manage.notify.what: Each gift is sent to your web address the moment PayPal completes it: who gave, what it paid for, and the check it keeps.
manage.notify.why: Zapier's Catch Hook turns that into a text, an email or a spreadsheet row, so the family knows to say thank you.
manage.notify.technical: POST with JSON (event gift.received or gift.test) and a Giftwise-Signature header: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<HMAC-SHA256 of "t.body" with the page's secret>. HTTPS only; addresses that resolve to private networks are refused.

page.verify.title: Check a report
page.verify.what: Every report to Social Security carries a code. This page rebuilds the report from Giftwise's records, asks PayPal for each payment in it, and checks the audit ledger.
page.verify.why: A caseworker or benefits counselor can confirm each gift went to the shop or ABLE account the report names, without logging in and without trusting a printout.
page.verify.technical: /v/{slug}/{month}/{code}. The code is 50 bits of SHA-256 over the report's facts in Crockford base 32. Payments are read with GET /v2/checkout/orders/{id} and GET /v1/payments/payouts/{batch}; the ledger is checked with verifyChain().

page.report.title: The report to Social Security
page.report.what: People on SSI tell Social Security about changes in income, including help from family and friends, by the 10th of the next month. Giftwise writes that report from the gifts themselves.
page.report.why: Every gift was checked by the rules before PayPal moved the money, so each line can say whether it changes the check, and show the PayPal record that proves where the money went.
page.report.technical: buildReport() in src/lib/report/ssa.ts runs the rules engine over every gift on the page (sample year, PayPal captures and PayPal Payouts items), applies the quarterly exclusion across months, and dates the deadline by 20 CFR 416.714(a). Also at GET /api/v1/ssa-report and the get_ssa_report MCP tool.

page.calendar.title: Benefit calendar
page.calendar.what: Every gift on the day it arrived, the day each report to Social Security is due, and the check each 1st of the month pays.
page.calendar.why: SSI counts income by calendar month and gives the $60 exclusion for one-time gifts once per quarter, so the day a gift lands can change the check. Move a gift to see it.
page.calendar.technical: Bryntum Calendar 7.3 (trial) in month and agenda views, with drag to move and a form that does the same without dragging. Each move reruns planMonths() from the rules engine in the browser. The theme follows the site's light and dark mode.

report.tell.title: What to tell Social Security
report.tell.what: Gifts that change income this month: cash, and housing costs someone else paid. Each comes with the sentence to say on the call.
report.tell.why: Reporting them on time keeps the check right and avoids a deduction for a late report.
report.tell.technical: A line goes here when the gift is cash, or classify() returns ism_shelter (rent, mortgage, property tax or utilities paid to the supplier). Counted income is countableIncome for the month minus the same month with no gifts.

report.records.title: For your records
report.records.what: Gifts that are not income, each with the rule that says so and the PayPal payment behind it.
report.records.why: If Social Security asks about help from family, these show the money went to the shop or the ABLE account, not to the person.
report.records.technical: Evidence is the PayPal capture id from Orders v2 (linked to its public receipt) or the transaction id of a PayPal Payouts item. Sample-year gifts have no PayPal record and say so.

report.how.title: How to report
report.how.what: Call Social Security, use the TTY line, or visit or write any Social Security office. The call script lists exactly what to say.
report.how.why: The script is written from the gifts, so nothing is left out and nothing extra is said.
report.how.technical: Phone numbers and wording are quoted from SSA pages and 20 CFR 416.708, 416.714 and 416.724, stored word for word in content/reporting.json.

judges.nightly.title: Checked every night
judges.nightly.what: Every night a Render Workflow checks the hosted demo from outside: each page a judge opens, each public API promise, and each failure case against the PayPal sandbox.
judges.nightly.why: A demo that is checked every night stays working through judging. If something breaks, the run says what and where before anyone else finds it.
judges.nightly.technical: workflows/src/main.ts: nightlyCheck fans out one Render Workflows task per check (runCase, checkPage, checkApi) with ctx.run, each with 2 retries (5 s, then 10 s), and files the run with POST /api/checks using a shared CHECKS_SECRET. A Render cron job starts it nightly with the Render SDK's workflows.startTask; Run the checks now does the same from POST /api/checks/start.

page.report.easy.title: Easy Read report
page.report.easy.what: The month's report written for the person who gets SSI, in English or Spanish: the answer first, then each gift in one short sentence with a picture beside it, what to do, and what to say on the call.
page.report.easy.why: The full report is written for a family member or counselor. The person on SSI is the one who must report, and about 851,000 people on SSI under 65 have an intellectual disability (SSA, December 2024). Social Security serves Spanish speakers on its main line (press 7).
page.report.easy.technical: easyRead() in src/lib/report/easy.ts writes every sentence from the same buildReport() data as the full report, with no model involved, following ASAN's Easy Read guide (one idea per line, about 10 to 15 words). A unit test holds every sentence to 15 words or fewer in both languages. /g/{slug}/report/reminder serves an .ics file: the due date with an alert three days before, and a monthly look on the 5th. Also at /api/v1/ssa-report?format=easy&lang=es.

page.monthly.title: Your monthly gift
page.monthly.what: The same amount every month. Each month Giftwise routes it again for that month's needs, shows what changed and why, and you approve that month in PayPal.
page.monthly.why: Help like rent or the electric bill comes back every month, while one-time needs get paid off. Routing each month again keeps every dollar going where it does not lower the check.
page.monthly.technical: src/lib/monthly.ts. needsForMonth() reopens recurring needs with what they received for that month and drops paid one-time needs; routeGift() routes the amount; diffPlans() writes what changed. The order route runs the rules again when you approve, and creates one Orders v2 order with a purchase unit and payee per recipient. Each month is written to the audit ledger (monthly.planned).

monthly.why.title: Why not charge automatically
monthly.why.what: Each month you approve the payment in PayPal yourself.
monthly.why.why: Giftwise never holds the money. An automatic charge would have to pay Giftwise first and pass it on.
monthly.why.technical: Tested in PayPal's sandbox on 2026-11-04: a PayPal wallet saved with Vault (store_in_vault ON_SUCCESS) on a multi-payee order works, but a later order with payment_source.paypal.vault_id and a third-party payee returns 422 BILLING_AGREEMENT_NOT_FOUND, and several third-party purchase units return VALIDATION_ERROR. A vaulted charge succeeds only when the platform is the payee. Signed in to PayPal, a giver approves a new multi-payee order in two clicks.

judges.field_cases.title: Real cases, from federal courts
judges.field_cases.what: SSI cases where SSA counted help from family or friends and a federal court reviewed the decision. Giftwise ran each one through its rules engine and compared the outcome with what SSA and the court held.
judges.field_cases.why: A benchmark Giftwise wrote proves the code does what was intended. Real decisions show the rules are right about the world, and what the same help would have kept if it had been routed differently.
judges.field_cases.technical: content/eval/field-cases.json holds 36 cases from GovInfo's USCOURTS collection (public domain, 17 U.S.C. 105), 14 scored. scripts/run-field-cases.ts runs each through planMonths() at 2026 rates and re-runs the help as Giftwise would route it (vendor, or ABLE only where the opinion shows disability before 46). Results in content/eval/field-cases-results.json. GoFundMe and Givebutter campaign pages were not used: their terms rule out automated reading.

stack.render-jobs.title: Render Workflows
stack.render-jobs.what: Runs the background jobs: each monthly gift is planned on the 1st, and the rulebook's search index is rebuilt every week.
stack.render-jobs.why: Each giver's page already shows that month's split before anyone opens it.
stack.render-jobs.technical: monthlyRun fans out one planMonthly task per active monthly gift, each with its own retries; rulebookIndex rebuilds the Elastic index. A nightly Render cron starts them with the Render SDK.

stack.channel3.title: Channel3
stack.channel3.what: The gift finder: real products for a need, each checked against the SSI rules before it can go on a page.
stack.channel3.why: The organizer can add a real item in a few taps, and gift cards that would count like cash are held back.
stack.channel3.technical: POST /v1/search with stock and price filters, from the organizer's view and the find_gift MCP tool. Without a key, a sample catalog stands in.

stack.elastic.title: Elasticsearch
stack.elastic.what: Ask the rulebook: finds the passages from the regulations and Social Security's manual that answer a question.
stack.elastic.why: Every answer comes with the exact passages it was drawn from, and each quote is checked word for word.
stack.elastic.technical: Hybrid retrieval (multi_match plus semantic_text with jina-embeddings-v3), fused by reciprocal rank, then reranked by jina-reranker-v3. Without Elastic, an in-app BM25 ranking stands in.

stack.postman.title: Postman
stack.postman.what: The Giftwise API as a collection anyone can import and run, with tests on every request.
stack.postman.why: A developer can try every endpoint in a minute, and the same collection runs in the test suite.
stack.postman.technical: 16 requests in five folders, run in the test suite with Newman.

stack.zapier.title: Zapier
stack.zapier.what: Can text or email the family the moment a gift arrives.
stack.zapier.why: The organizer hears about each gift without opening the page.
stack.zapier.technical: Each PayPal capture posts a signed gift.received event to the organizer's webhook; a Zapier Catch Hook turns it into a text, an email or a spreadsheet row. HMAC-SHA256 signatures with a timestamp.

stack.rules-watch.title: Federal Register watch
stack.rules-watch.what: Checks the Federal Register for new rules about SSI income and help with housing, and for each year's new SSI amounts.
stack.rules-watch.why: When Social Security changes a rule or an amount, Giftwise sees it, so the answers stay current.
stack.rules-watch.technical: Federal Register API queries for 20 CFR Part 416 rules that mention in-kind support and maintenance or unearned income, and SSA cost-of-living notices (src/lib/rules-watch.ts). Runs on the Status page and nightly in the outside checks.
